title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 180B — blazux vLLM hybrid mmap build
slug_note: The memory-efficiency specialist: ~122GB on disk but only ~76GB resident, thanks to hybrid FP8 sides and mmap. Vision stays on. Reported ~26-31 tok/s.

variation.quant_detail: Hybrid quantization: FP8 on the sides, lower precision elsewhere. Roughly +20% throughput from the hybrid FP8 sides alone.

engine.config: vLLM with mmap-backed weight loading. ~122GB on disk compresses to ~76GB resident.

requirements.notes: Lowest resident footprint of the full-featured 180B builds — about 43GB of headroom left on a 128GB box, versus ~15GB for Mia's.

caveats: Slower than azampatti and Mia on throughput; the trade is resident memory and working vision.

The Saren fork reports substantially better numbers (47.5 code / 60 JSON) on the same approach. Fork-versus-upstream deltas this large are usually a configuration difference, not a code difference — verify which one you are actually installing.
The 2,904 tok/s figure in the repo is prefill throughput at a 32K prompt with the deterministic top-k kernel, not decode; excluded from the measurements.
DET_TOPK=1 deterministic top-k is what makes his kernel-level numbers reproducible; without it GB10 top-k is non-deterministic run to run.
The checkpoint card states no license field; the weights lineage is Qwen Apache-2.0.
Builder runtimes carry their own terms on top of the weights (Mia's scripts are AGPL-3.0).
